source.note: Hypertension: start 10 mg once daily, usual 20-40 mg; 2.5 mg starts appear in 2.2-2.4; max 40 mg once daily (2.2, 2.4). 'Doses up to 80 mg have been used but do not appear to give greater effect.'
'mean extent of absorption ... approximately 25%, with large intersubject variability (6% to 60%)'; model = the stated mean 0.25
'effective half-life of 12 hours' on multiple dosing
'peak serum concentrations ... occur within about 7 hours'

source.citation: Sandra L, Degraeuwe E, De Bruyne P, et al. Population pharmacokinetics of lisinopril in hypertensive children and adolescents with normal to mildly reduced kidney function. Br J Clin Pharmacol. 2024;90(2):504-515. doi:10.1111/bcp.15936
source.note: No US label, Health Canada monograph, or adult PK paper found gives a Vd number (Beermann 1988, Am J Med, gives bioavailability/half-life but no Vd). This population-PK study reports 'volume of distribution (31.38 L 70 kg-1 [10.5, 52.3])' in pediatric patients; converted to L/kg by dividing by 70. The label notes pediatric PK 'are similar to those obtained previously in adults,' so used here as the best available estimate pending an adult-specific number.

'does not undergo metabolism and is excreted unchanged entirely in the urine' (fractions are of the absorbed drug). MISSING: no US label, Health Canada monograph or PubMed abstract checked gives a volume of distribution.

journey.text: Only about a quarter of a dose is absorbed from the gut, and this varies a lot between people; levels peak about 7 hours later.
Blocks ACE, an enzyme that makes angiotensin II, a hormone that tightens blood vessels. Vessels relax and blood pressure drops.
Not broken down at all: it leaves unchanged in urine.
